mainTopic: Does the פסוק about slaughtering for idols (זובח לאלהים) teach a general rule, or is it needed to teach the case of slaughtering with intent for a later idolatrous act? The sugya tests this through the מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a disagreement between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. The case is an animal slaughtered with a plan to sprinkle its blood or burn its fats for an idol. רבא בר רב חנן uses that disagreement to question a ברייתא that learns a general rule about idol worship from the פסוק about slaughter. רב פפא and רב אחא בריה דרב איקא each push back on him from opposite sides. רב אחא brings the case of someone who bows to a mountain: the mountain stays permitted, but the worshipper is executed. Next the גמרא asks what ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ leaves out according to רבא בר רב חנן. The answer is defecating before מרקוליס. The גמרא then answers a challenge from רבי אליעזר's פסוק about sacrificing to מרקוליס by saying that פסוק is about sacrificing to spite the Torah. A new section begins when רבה raises a contradiction between two משניות: is a person liable just for saying 'I will worship' an idol? רב המנונא answers by separating the cases. רב יוסף first explains the contradiction as a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, then takes that explanation back. The amud ends with a new explanation of their dispute: do people sincerely say 'Yes' to someone who calls them to worship himself? The quote of what the people say to themselves continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The two opinions on the animal slaughtered with idolatrous intent
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the מחלוקת: according to רבי יוחנן, benefit from the animal is forbidden; ריש לקיש says it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Benefit from the animal] is forbidden. And ריש לקיש says: it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a disagreement from just before this point. The case is someone who slaughters an animal while planning to use its blood or fats for an idol. רבי יוחנן says the animal becomes forbidden, and ריש לקיש says it stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case involves one act of service (slaughter) done with a plan for a different act of service (sprinkling or burning). This is called מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה. For רבי יוחנן the plan counts, so the animal is forbidden. For ריש לקיש it does not count, so the animal is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden (here: forbidden to get any benefit from it)
Permitted
Intention from one act of service to another: doing one act while planning another
ריש לקיש, the usual disputant of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: is forbidden,
and Reish Lakish says: it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the מחלוקת that רבא בר רב חנן brought to back up his challenge to the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: an animal slaughtered with intent to sprinkle its blood or burn its fats for an idol is forbidden. ריש לקיש: it is permitted.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן but not ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן concludes that the ברייתא's lesson works for רבי יוחנן. For ריש לקיש, though, the פסוק is needed for its own case.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי יוחנן. But for ריש לקיש, the פסוק is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן finishes his challenge. The ברייתא's way of learning from the פסוק only works if you follow רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learns the rule of intention from one act to another from a different source. So for him, the slaughter פסוק is free to teach a general rule, as the ברייתא says. ריש לקיש has no other source for that case, so he needs this פסוק for it. That leaves nothing extra for the ברייתא's general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out well (for this view)
He needs a פסוק (for something else)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the twist: ריש לקיש is the one who permits the animal, yet he is the one who 'needs' the פסוק. For him, the פסוק is the only source that this kind of intention matters at all.

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Yoḥanan,
but according to Reish Lakish, he needs the verse.
phrases.notes: The verse is זובח לאלהים יחרם (שמות 22:19), which the ברייתא used to learn its general rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֶלָּא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ בָּעֵי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מחלוקת in step 1 to challenge the ברייתא's lesson.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that learns a general rule from the slaughter פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק can only teach a general rule if it is not needed for its own case. For ריש לקיש it is needed, so the ברייתא's lesson fails for him.

steps.title: רב פפא: even for רבי יוחנן the פסוק is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that רבי יוחנן only forbids the animal. Without the פסוק, the person would not get the death penalty, so the פסוק is needed even for רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא challenged: And for רבי יוחנן, is no פסוק needed? רבי יוחנן only forbids the animal, but the man would not deserve death! So the פסוק comes to make the man liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks the 'it works for רבי יוחנן' part of step 2. He says the פסוק is needed for רבי יוחנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making the animal forbidden is one thing, and executing the person is another. רבי יוחנן's other source only shows that the animal is forbidden. The death penalty for the person still needs this פסוק. So the ברייתא's lesson would fail according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (strongly objected)
He only went so far as to forbid…
The man (the person who did the act)
Liable to death

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to this:
And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, is the verse not needed?

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא אָסַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan only prohibits

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה, אֲבָל גַּבְרָא לָא בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא!
phrases.english: the animal, but the man is not liable to death!
And the verse comes to make the man liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא בָּעֵי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the claim in step 2 that the ברייתא works for רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'הניחא לרבי יוחנן' half of step 2
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It mixed up forbidding the animal with making the person liable to death. Only the פסוק gives the death penalty.

steps.title: רב אחא: even for ריש לקיש the person is liable without the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא argues the other way. ריש לקיש only permits the animal, but the person is still liable to death, so ריש לקיש does not need the פסוק either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא challenged: And for ריש לקיש, is a פסוק needed? ריש לקיש only permits the animal, but the man is liable to death!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא attacks the 'ריש לקיש needs the פסוק' part of step 2. He uses the same split between animal and person that רב פפא used, but in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal being permitted does not mean the person is innocent. ריש לקיש's ruling is only about the animal, so the person's death penalty can stand without this פסוק. That makes the פסוק extra, and the ברייתא's general lesson works again.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits
Is a פסוק really needed? (expecting the answer no)

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, objects to this:
And according to Reish Lakish, is the verse needed?

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָא שָׁרֵי רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Reish Lakish only permits

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּהֵמָה, אֲבָל גַּבְרָא בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא!
phrases.english: the animal, but the man is liable to death!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מִי בָּעֵי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposite direction from step 3: rather than saying everyone needs the פסוק, it says even ריש לקיש does not.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'ריש לקיש בעי קרא' half of step 2, which was רבא בר רב חנן's challenge
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed that permitting the animal means the person is not liable. The two are separate.

steps.title: Proof from bowing to a mountain
steps.stepSummary: Someone who bows to a mountain is executed by the sword, yet the mountain stays permitted. This shows a person can be liable even when the object is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like one who bows to a mountain: the mountain is permitted, and the one who worships it is executed by the sword.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא backs up his point from step 4 with a clear example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mountain is attached to the ground, so it does not become forbidden even when someone worships it. Still, the worshipper gets the death penalty. In the same way, ריש לקיש's permitted animal does not stop the slaughterer from being liable to death.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like…
One who bows down to a mountain
Sword, one of the four death penalties of בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: Whether an object is forbidden and whether a person is liable to death are separate questions. רב פפא uses this split to say both views need the פסוק. רב אחא uses it, with the mountain as proof, to say neither view needs it.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the slaughter פסוק is extra for both views, the ברייתא's general rule is saved. That rule decides which acts of idol worship carry the death penalty.

phrases.english: It is just like one who bows to a mountain,
where the mountain is permitted, yet the one who worships it is executed by the sword.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for רב אחא's claim in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can be liable to death even when the object of worship stays permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted rule that a mountain someone bowed to is permitted, while the worshipper is executed by the sword

steps.title: What does the verse 'how do they serve' leave out?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי asks רבינא: according to רבא בר רב חנן, השתחואה already teaches about all honorable worship, so what is ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ needed to leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדפתי said to רבינא: According to what רבא בר רב חנן told אביי, that bowing was singled out to teach about the whole group, what does ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב אחא מדפתי asks what job the פסוק ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ has left if we follow רבא בר רב חנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר רב חנן said that השתחואה was singled out in the פסוק to teach a rule for every honorable kind of worship. If that is true, the פסוק ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ (liable only for the way the idol is normally served) seems to have nothing left to exclude. The question is: what case does it leave out?

keyTerms.meaning: Bowing down, a form of worship
Was singled out to teach about the whole group
"How do they serve", the פסוק about worshipping an idol in its usual way
To leave out what?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאי דְּקָאָמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי,
phrases.english: According to what Rava bar Rav Chanan said to Abaye,
"Say that bowing was singled out
phrases.notes: This is רבא בר רב חנן's earlier idea, quoted again here.

phrases.english: to teach about the entire group,"
then "how do they serve" comes to leave out what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about רבא בר רב חנן's reading of the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר רב חנן's claim that השתחואה teaches about every honorable kind of worship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If השתחואה already covers the whole group, the פסוק ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ seems to have nothing left to exclude.

steps.title: Defecating before a sacrifice-idol is already excluded by bowing
steps.stepSummary: A possible answer is that ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ leaves out defecating before an idol that is served with sacrifices. This is rejected, because the lesson of השתחואה already leaves that case out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it leaves out someone who defecates before an idol served by sacrifices, that is already learned from bowing. Just as bowing is an honorable act, so too only honorable acts count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one answer to the question and then pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Defecating is a degrading act, not an honorable one. Since השתחואה teaches that only honorable acts carry liability, this case is already left out. So ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ cannot be needed for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say
One who exposes himself to defecate
It is already learned from bowing
An honorable way of serving

phrases.english: And if you would say:
It leaves out one who defecates before an idol served by sacrifices?
That is already learned from bowing!
Just as bowing is an honorable act,
so too, anything that is an honorable act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to Step 6 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ excludes defecating before a sacrifice-idol
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That case is already excluded by the lesson of השתחואה, because only honorable acts count.

steps.title: The verse leaves out defecating before מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: The real answer: ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ leaves out defecating before מרקוליס. Without the פסוק, we might think that since מרקוליס is normally served in a degrading way, any degrading act would count.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it leaves out someone who defecates before מרקוליס. You might have thought: since its worship is degrading, any degrading act counts. The פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the accepted answer to רב אחא מדפתי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרקוליס is unusual because its normal worship is itself degrading. So we might think any degrading act, like defecating, would count as worship for it. ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ teaches that a person is liable only for the way מרקוליס is actually served.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol whose normal worship was degrading
It might enter your mind to say
Degradation, a disrespectful act
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: Rather, it leaves out one who defecates before Markulis.
phrases.notes: The normal worship of מרקוליס was throwing stones at it, which is an insulting act.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since its worship is a degrading act,
so too, any degrading act counts?
The verse teaches us that it does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 7 with a working answer to Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a unique case that the lesson of השתחואה does not cover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מרקוליס is served by a degrading act, any degrading act would count as its worship.
steps.terutzMaskana: For מרקוליס, a person is liable only for its actual normal worship, not for other degrading acts.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבא בר רב חנן, השתחואה teaches about all honorable worship, and ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ is still needed for the special case of מרקוליס.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's verse for sacrificing to מרקוליס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי אליעזר's teaching that a separate פסוק is needed to make someone liable for sacrificing an animal to מרקוליס. This sets up a new difficulty for רבא בר רב חנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רבי אליעזר said: From where do we know that one who sacrifices an animal to מרקוליס is liable? As it says: "And they shall no longer sacrifice their sacrifices to the satyrs."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes רבי אליעזר's teaching, and the full difficulty against רבא בר רב חנן comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sacrificing is an honorable act of worship. According to רבא בר רב חנן, the lesson of השתחואה should already make it count, even for מרקוליס. Yet רבי אליעזר brings a separate פסוק for it, which suggests he did not learn it from השתחואה.

keyTerms.meaning: But what about that which (he) said
From where do we know?
One who sacrifices
Satyrs, a kind of idol or demon

phrases.english: But what about that which Rabbi Eliezer said:
From where do we know that one who sacrifices an animal to Markulis
is liable?
As it is stated: "And they shall no longer sacrifice
their sacrifices to the satyrs."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in Step 8, the גמרא raises a new challenge to רבא בר רב חנן's approach.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר רב חנן's reading that השתחואה teaches about every honorable kind of worship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If השתחואה already covers sacrificing, why does רבי אליעזר need a separate פסוק to make someone liable for sacrificing to מרקוליס?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר finishes his derivation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the extra פסוק about sacrificing is not needed for an idol normally served by sacrifices, since ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ already covers that. So it must teach about an idol not normally served that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק is not needed for an idol served in its normal way, since that is already written in ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״, then use it for an idol served not in its normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes רבי אליעזר's teaching from the previous step. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אֵיכָה יַעַבְדוּ״ already makes someone liable for serving an idol in its own normal way. So the extra פסוק about sacrificing must have a new job: making someone liable for sacrificing even to an idol like מרקוליס, which is not normally served with sacrifices.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter (a method of moving a פסוק to another lesson)
In its normal way of being served
Not in its normal way of being served
Apply it to another matter

phrases.english: If it is not needed for the matter of serving an idol in its normal way,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the separate פסוק about sacrificing that רבי אליעזר brought in the previous step.

phrases.english: since it is already written: "How do they serve",
apply it to the matter of serving it not in its normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of רבי אליעזר's teaching that began in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra פסוק about sacrificing makes one liable for sacrificing even to an idol not normally served by sacrifices.

steps.title: But רבא בר רב חנן learns this from bowing
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא בר רב חנן, liability for worship not in the idol's normal way already comes from השתחואה, so רבי אליעזר's extra פסוק would be unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But serving an idol not in its normal way is already learned from bowing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא בר רב חנן using רבי אליעזר's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר רב חנן said השתחואה teaches liability for any honorable worship, even if it is not the idol's usual worship. If so, why would רבי אליעזר need a separate פסוק to teach the same thing about sacrificing to מרקוליס?

keyTerms.meaning: Bowing down
It is learned from

phrases.english: Serving not in its normal way
is already learned from bowing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's derivation to attack רבא בר רב חנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא בר רב חנן's view that השתחואה teaches all honorable forms of worship
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If השתחואה already teaches this, רבי אליעזר's extra פסוק would teach nothing new.

steps.title: The פסוק is about sacrificing to spite
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר's פסוק is about someone who sacrifices to מרקוליס not to worship it but to spite the Torah. That case cannot be learned from השתחואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about one who sacrifices to spite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying רבי אליעזר's פסוק teaches a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: השתחואה teaches about someone who really means to worship. רבי אליעזר's פסוק adds that even someone who sacrifices only to spite the Torah's prohibition is liable. So both sources are needed, and רבא בר רב חנן stands.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters or sacrifices
To spite, to act defiantly

phrases.english: There, it is about one who sacrifices to spite.
phrases.notes: 'There' means רבי אליעזר's פסוק. The person is not trying to worship; he is deliberately defying the Torah's prohibition.

steps.whatToRemember: השתחואה teaches liability for real worship in any honorable way. רבי אליעזר's פסוק adds liability even for sacrificing just to spite the Torah.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case of the other source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר's פסוק seemed to teach liability for sacrificing as worship to an idol not normally served that way, which השתחואה already covers.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches liability for sacrificing to spite, which השתחואה does not cover.

steps.title: רבה meets רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: A new section opens. רב המנונא lost his oxen, and רבה met him and raised a contradiction between two משניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא's oxen got lost. רבה met him and set two משניות against each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a short story. It is setting up the contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here yet. The story tells us who asked whom, and that the question will be a contradiction between two משניות.

keyTerms.meaning: Got lost
Oxen
He set against, raised a contradiction
Against each other

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna's oxen got lost.
Rabba met him,
and raised before him a contradiction between משניות:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבה's contradiction between two משניות.

steps.title: Is saying 'I will worship' punishable?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה says 'one who worships,' which suggests only doing counts, not saying. But another משנה makes one liable for saying 'I will worship' or 'Let us go and worship.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'one who worships an idol' — doing, yes; saying, no. But didn't we learn: 'One who says I will worship, I will go and worship, let us go and worship' is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה points out that two משניות seem to contradict each other about whether just saying you will worship an idol makes you liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the word 'worships' in our משנה we infer that only an act of worship brings liability. Yet another משנה lists people who only speak about worshipping as liable. Both cannot be true as they stand, so an answer is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
But didn't we learn?
I will worship

steps.confusionAlert: Our משנה does not say outright that speaking is exempt. That is only inferred from its choice of the word 'worships.'

phrases.english: We learned: "One who worships an idol"
one who worships, yes; one who says, no.
But didn't we learn:
"One who says: 'I will worship,' 'I will go and worship,'
'Let us go and worship'" is liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the contradiction that step 13 announced.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two משניות: one implying only doing counts, the other making speaking liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from one משנה's wording ('worships') contradicts an explicit list in another משנה that makes speech alone punishable.

steps.title: רב המנונא: our case is someone who accepts the idol only through worship
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא resolves the contradiction. Our משנה is about someone who says he will accept the idol only by actually worshiping it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our משנה is talking about someone who says, 'I am not accepting this idol as my god except through worship.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers רבה's contradiction from the last step. He explains that the two משניות are talking about different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person in our משנה has decided that his acceptance of the idol will only happen through an act of worship. So for him, nothing counts until he actually worships. Someone who accepts the idol right away with words is a different case, and he is liable for speech alone.

keyTerms.meaning: I accept it upon myself (as a god)
worship, an actual act of service
in a case where he says

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב המנונא answering רבה.

phrases.english: It is a case of one who says: "I do not accept it upon myself
except through worship."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּאוֹמֵר ״אֵינִי מְקַבְּלוֹ עָלַי אֶלָּא בַּעֲבוֹדָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each משנה describes a different intention of the worshiper.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to say that speech never makes one liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Speech does make one liable. Our משנה is only about a person who ties his acceptance to an actual act of worship.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two משניות follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says there is no need for רב המנונא's answer. The contradiction comes from a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about one who says 'Come and worship me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Did you take the תנאים out of the world? This is a dispute between תנאים. A ברייתא teaches that if someone says 'Come and worship me,' רבי מאיר holds him liable and רבי יהודה exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a different answer to the contradiction. He says each משנה simply follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining both משניות according to one view, רב יוסף says they disagree with each other. The source is a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about a person who calls on others to worship him. The next step explains exactly what they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Tannaim, the sages of the משנה period
you removed from the world
come and worship me
holds liable / exempts

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Have you removed the Tannaim from the world?
phrases.notes: He means: why work so hard to make both משניות agree? Just say two תנאים disagree.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim, as it is taught:
One who says, "Come and worship me":
Rabbi Meir holds him liable,
and Rabbi Yehuda exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the step 14 contradiction, instead of רב המנונא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each משנה to a different תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות must follow one view, so the cases must be split.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משניות simply follow two different תנאים.

steps.title: What exactly רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about
steps.stepSummary: If people actually worshiped him, everyone agrees he is liable. They only argue when it stayed as words: רבי מאיר says speech counts, and רבי יהודה says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the people actually worshiped him, everyone agrees he is liable, as the פסוק says, 'You shall not make for yourself a graven image.' They only argue when there was just talk. רבי מאיר holds that speech is significant. רבי יהודה holds that speech is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the exact point of the argument in the ברייתא. This shows how it matches the two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When real worship happened, both agree he is liable. The argument is only about words with no action. So רבי יהודה, who says speech is nothing, fits our משנה. רבי מאיר, who says speech counts, fits the other משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: they worshiped
everyone agrees
mere speech
it is something (significant)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: speech alone counts. רבי יהודה: speech alone does not count. Both agree he is liable if actual worship happened.

phrases.english: Where they actually worshiped him,
everyone agrees (that he is liable),
as it is written: "You shall not make for yourself a graven image."
Where they disagree is in a case of mere speech.
Rabbi Meir holds:
speech is a significant matter,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds:
speech is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דִּפְלַחוּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 16, narrowing the dispute to speech alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone agrees he is liable when actual worship happened. In a case of speech alone, רבי מאיר says liable and רבי יהודה says exempt.

steps.title: רב יוסף takes back his answer: even רבי יהודה counts speech
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף retracts. A משנה shows that רבי יהודה himself makes one liable for saying 'I will worship,' so speech does count for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף later said: What I said is not right. Even רבי יהודה makes one liable for speech. We learned that רבי יהודה says: One is never liable until he says 'I will worship,' 'I will go and worship,' or 'Let us go and worship.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rejects his own answer from the last two steps. He brings a משנה where רבי יהודה makes a person liable just for words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer depended on רבי יהודה holding that speech is nothing. But this משנה quotes רבי יהודה making a person liable for saying 'I will worship,' which is only speech. So the contradiction cannot be explained as רבי מאיר against רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: he later said again (changed his mind)
what I said is not correct
I will worship
let us go and worship

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not answered by someone else here. He is rejecting his own earlier answer.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef then said:
What I said is not correct,
for even according to Rabbi Yehuda,
he holds one liable for speech as well.
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One is never liable
unless he says, "I will worship,"
"I will go and worship," or "Let us go and worship."

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of steps 16 and 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the two משניות follow רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהודה himself makes one liable for speech alone, so he cannot be the source of the view that only actual worship counts.

steps.title: So what do they really argue about?
steps.stepSummary: Since speech counts for both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the גמרא asks what their dispute is really about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a fresh question: if the dispute is not about whether words count, what is it about? This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18, רב יוסף's explanation fell apart because רבי יהודה also holds that speech counts. That leaves the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about 'Come and worship me' without an explanation. The גמרא now looks for a new basis for it.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (The standard question asking for the real point of a dispute)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, in their argument about someone who says "Come and worship me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the retraction in Step 18, the גמרא looks for a new basis for the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the real point of disagreement between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about one who says 'Come and worship me'?

steps.title: They argue about one who calls others to worship himself
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is about a מסית who urges others to worship him, and the others answer 'Yes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about one who incites others to worship himself, and the people answer him, 'Yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dispute is about a specific case. Someone tries to get others to worship him, and they answer 'Yes.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new answer moves the dispute away from the person speaking. It is now about the people who answer him. The question is no longer whether words can make someone liable. It is whether these listeners' 'Yes' counts as a real acceptance.

keyTerms.meaning: One who incites or persuades others to worship an idol
To himself. Here it means the person is urging others to worship him.
Yes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the case is about the person himself saying 'I will worship.' Here he is calling on OTHERS to worship him, and the question is about THEIR 'Yes.'

phrases.english: In the case of one who incites others to worship himself
and they say to him "Yes" — about this they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמֵסִית לְעַצְמוֹ וְאָמְרִי לֵיהּ אִין קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19 by stating the exact case they argue about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is about a person who urges others to worship him and they answer 'Yes.'

steps.title: Do people take such a person seriously?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says people listen to one who calls them to worship himself, so their 'Yes' is sincere. רבי יהודה says people do not listen to him, and the גמרא begins to quote what they say to themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master (רבי מאיר) holds that when someone urges others to worship him, they do listen to him, and the 'Yes' they say is real. The other master (רבי יהודה) holds that they do not listen to him, because they say to themselves:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning on each side. רבי מאיר thinks the people's 'Yes' is real. רבי יהודה thinks it is not. The line ends by starting to quote what the people say to themselves, and that quote continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is now about human nature. Do people really accept a man who claims to be a god? For רבי מאיר they do, so their 'Yes' is a real acceptance. For רבי יהודה they do not take him seriously. The reason why is about to be given in the people's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds (introduces one side of a dispute)
They listen to him (they take him seriously)
Truth, sincere
For they say (introduces what people think to themselves)

steps.whatToRemember: The new explanation: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה do not argue about whether speech counts. They argue about whether people sincerely answer 'Yes' to someone who calls them to worship himself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns a legal question about speech into a factual question about how people react. That makes it possible for both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה to agree that speech counts.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר, מֵסִית לְעַצְמוֹ – שָׁמְעִי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: One master holds: one who incites others to worship himself — they listen to him,
and the "Yes" that they say to him is sincere;

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר, מֵסִית לְעַצְמוֹ – לָא שָׁמְעִי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and the other master holds: one who incites others to worship himself — they do not listen to him,
for they say:

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר, מֵסִית לְעַצְמוֹ – שָׁמְעִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out each side's reasoning for the case named in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: people listen to one who calls them to worship himself, so their 'Yes' is sincere. רבי יהודה: people do not listen to him.
